title: Britain's Most Haunted Construction Sites
content:
Spooky season has arrived. 

Halloween is just around the corner, and hauntings are the topic of discussion. Whether you’re a believer or a sceptic, you've probably heard of a couple of unusual cases that are hard to explain. Typically, we’d be looking at haunted houses and the like. 

But this is Fix Radio, and we’re doing things differently. So, instead of standard buildings, we’re looking at construction sites that are reported to have been the home to ghosts, ghouls, and things that lurk in the shadows. These are some of Britain’s most haunted construction sites, and we guarantee you probably wouldn’t want to work on them. 

Birmingham City Centre

Anchored by the new HS2 station, Birmingham City Centre is still undergoing major renovation works to the tune of £1.9 billion. While it was a complex job to begin with, what labourers have experienced has left them spooked. 

Reports have come in of a ghostly woman in a white dress spotted on CCTV footage, even when the site was locked down. While there have been efforts to debunk the myth with statements that it was a real woman walking through the shot, not everyone is convinced. 

National Construction College

The National Construction College in Bircham Newton was once a WWI and WWII RAF base, but it had been modified to meet the demands of contemporary users. Some of that history still persists in the walls, as trainees began to experience odd occurrences. 

The paranormal activity that construction workers felt there was so vast that they stopped operations for a time and allowed the BBC to film a special investigation. It was Block A that experienced the most activity, with phantom footsteps, the sounds of heavy machinery, and even poltergeist sightings scaring workers. 

Kelvedon Hatch Nuclear Bunker 

In the early 1950s, the Kelvedon Hatch Nuclear Bunker was built in Essex, a massive subterranean system that felt much-needed as the Cold War heated up. It was during its construction that labourers started to notice genuinely disturbing things. 

With rumours that one workman had been swallowed whole by the concrete, with only his hat remaining, urban myths swept through the site. When the team accidentally unearthed an ancient burial ground, their unease grew and paranoia set in. Today, the bunker serves as a museum and tourist attraction and is still thought to be haunted. 

Have you ever noticed something strange on site?
